provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The canonical rule splits the input into a 3x3 arrangement of equal blocks, each of size h/3 by w/3. It outputs the top-right block unchanged. Cropping commutes with D4 transforms. So the transformed output is the block at the transformed corner of the visible grid, in visible orientation, with no re-rotation needed. The factory works out which corner the original top-right block lands on. A horizontal flip (d4 >= 4) sends TR to TL. Each clockwise rotation then moves corners TL -> TR -> BR -> BL. The emitted program crops that corner directly in visible coordinates, using block size h//3 by w//3. Colours are copied verbatim, so the palette needs no special handling.
draft_notes.limitations: The block position is fixed by the generator, not inferred from the demonstrations. Under the generator's domain, inputs are 9x9 grids and the blocks are 3x3. Non-multiple-of-3 grids are handled by floor division, flush to the chosen corner. That case lies outside the constructor's domain. The fixtures agree with the uniform rule, and no contradictions were found.
